Track 1: A clock is a device people use to tell time. The first known type of clock was the sundial. Over 3500 years ago, people in Egypt and Babylon measured time by observing where shadows from the sun fell across a raised spike in different directions throughout the day. People have also used dripping water, falling sand (in an hour glass), special candles, and even burning incense to keep track of the time. The first known mechanical clocks were made about 800 years ago and were powered by weights; we don't know who built the first one. Many clever people in England, Italy, and France were thinking about and working on clocks around the same time. Today, clocks come in many shapes and sizes. Some clocks can take up entire towers. Others, called watches, are small enough to be worn on a person’s finger or wrist. Clocks are one of the most commonly used tools around the world!
Track 2: Today, the two most common types of clocks are digital and analog. Digital clocks show time by displaying numbers on a screen. Analog clocks are circles with the numbers one through twelve spaced around the outer edge. Thin sticks called hands rotate from the center and point out at the numbers. On clocks with two hands, the shorter hand points out the hour, and the longer hand points out the minute. On clocks with three hands, you can use thickness to figure out which hand is which: the thickest hand points out the hour, medium points out the minute, and thinnest points out the second. And, sometimes the second hand is a different color. Every day, exactly at 12pm/noon and 12am/midnight, all of the hands on an analog clock are pointing straight up at the number 12. Often, when the power goes out or when someone unplugs and restarts a digital clock, it shows the time for midnight--zero zero zero or twelve zero zero–the start of a brand new calendar day.
